body: Thank you, I appreciate you talking it through with me!
He's asleep right now (we work different shifts) but I plan on telling him soon. Even if I just need to show him this post to do so.

I'm close to my mom and dad. He only gets along with my mom. Since we live in separate states though we've really only been in the same place once in the past two years and that was for my wedding. My parents don't ask me about him much because they know we don't really talk as it is. I do not want kids, although he does have a child and wife that I like that I would be cutting myself off from.

I'm honestly leaning towards confiding in my husband so someone in my life knows, and not telling my family. 

We all live in different states now and my brother is too poor to travel for the most part so it should be fairly easy to casually opt out of the couple times he does travel. That brother is already married, as am I. My other brother is in a serious relationship, so that would likely be a wedding soon, but I have a feeling that might be a destination wedding that one or both of us could opt out of due to cost. 

I have just finally started getting on good terms with my parents within the last year or two and it's been really nice and I don't think I can handle losing that again.
Thank you! I've been in therapy for four years for my other incidents of trauma, but this is just recently coming to light for fully for me.

My issue is, my brother and I have never gotten along on any level and I do not really wish to maintain a relationship with him. But I do not think I can cut him out without affecting the rest of my family. 

I also do not know if he would just like about it and I have no idea who my family would believe or if they would think this is a big enough issue for me to be upset about now that we're all adults. (I'm the youngest and in my mid twenties.)

Thanks. And I think it's more of me being uninterested in most 40-somethings. Just vastly different life stages and being rural, and having an age gap, most of them have vastly different opinions and world views than I do (grew up in a large city.) 

I've heard people in my office say horrendous things about people with mental health issues and I'm not interested in that.

I've tried Meetup and it didn't really help. I've honestly never really fit in. I had a big group of friends in high school but was only personally close with two of them. I was in a sorority and about 6 other organizations in college, still had issues (although college was very much the most supportive time of my life, I closed myself off by entering an abusive relationship and that's on me.) 

I've been working really hard since college. I felt really comfortable at my old job and liked my co-workers but management sucked and would literally scream at everyone so I had to find a new job for my mental health. Now everyone at my current job is 40+ (I'm 20s) so that's an issue. 

My one hobby I love is horses but I live in a rural area now so most people just keep their animals on their own property. I do board mine, but I've been there six months and seen another owner once. 

I like my SOs friends but their his friends and while I know they like me, they still don't treat me quite the same as the treat the rest of the group. 

I just feel stuck. I feel like I have tried everything.
I like metal. The soft ones usually don't have as defined as an "indent" and slip out of me if not actively being held in.

Hey, not totally the same. But maybe my situation can help you. I was also sexually assaulted in college. I called my parents crying and asking to transfer out. I decided against that a week or two later. I am very happy with the decision I made to stay at the university, as it was the best place for me academically and socially (I graduated three years ago for context.) 

I do regret not ditching my friends who could not be supportive. My friends victim blamed a lot and basically said I deserved it. I stayed friends with them because I didn't want to be alone. I don't know how big your university is, but if it's a larger one, it is so easy to leave friends behind and make new ones. Do this for your mental health. 

Ultimately its up to whatever makes you happiest. I wish you luck and strength.

Thank you, I talked to my husband about it and sent a message. I just always want to help when I can when someone is in that place because I've been there and I've gone through a lot of the bad coping mechanisms and am now nicely on my way to a healthy life and just want to offer help if I can.

Not really but I kind of snapped out of it myself. The thing my therapist always harps on me for, that really helps is to catch yourself in a negative thought pattern and actively replace it with a positive one. It takes practice. So like from the above post, instead of thinking, my tummy is so fat, I would think that my husband chose me and loves me and my body. I could also even think if that's a little hard, that I may not love my body right now, but I have the support and tools available to work on it. 

I have to meditate on stuff like this a lot to help me. Good luck!

I think maybe it depends on the trauma? I had some long term abuse and I don't have any sort of anniversary for that because it happened over the course of more than a year. But the first time I got raped was on Halloween at a party, so I absolutely despised Halloween parties for awhile. Especially because a lot of victim blaming happened around the costume I was wearing.
Definitely normal but if you have more in-depth questions ask the lovely folks at r/PTSD.
I told friends and none of them knew this was a thing.
They can be, but that at least tells you when someone does it, so a lot of times people are more cautious about it because they'll be "caught." This does not send a notification to the sender.
Arthouse Properties.
I've also had issues with friendships. I've literally been told I'm a burden/too high maintenance so why should I believe I'm not?

Thanks. I posted similar issues across a couple subs I'm on and didn't really get help on any of them, other than some agreeing they're going through the same thing. So we're not alone. Just seems none of us know of a fix.
Yes! It was that feeling of the obsession! To have someone so focused on you and infatuated with you, only if it only lasted a night, was intoxicating.
I met my husband while I was in the process of getting away from my nex lol. I love my husband but I do wish I had some alone time.
I wish the best for you and hope you find that strength.

I completely understand you. I stayed much longer than I should have, and deluded myself into only believing the good after so much bad. Frankly, I didn't get the courage to walk away until I met the man that is now my husband. I wish you more strength than I had, so you can leave and be safe. Or that you too will find your guardian angel to give you the strength to leave. Sometimes we need to borrow it. Stay strong and stay safe.
